text:
maria (AE): Heads up team — Cobalt Retail wants a short POC next week. Main asks: low-latency streaming chat, function/tool calls to our inventory service, and strict structured JSON outputs for downstream parsing. They also flagged pricing sensitivity and SOC2 questions. Can someone own the tech handoff?
jamie (SE): I can run the hookup. Need to confirm SDK language (they want Node + Python sample). Also: do they need SSE or websockets for streaming?
maria (AE): Node for the app, Python for backend batch. Prefer websockets but they said browser SSE might be easier for their engineers.
jamie (SE): Websockets + our streaming SDK works fine. For function calls — confirm expected RTT. If they want <200ms end-to-end we should use our dedicated variant or edge routing.
chris (Eng): @jamie what's their expected QPS? batching and KV-cache will change perf math. If <50 QPS, we can stay hosted with dedup cache. If bursts >200, recommend dedicated pool.
jamie (SE): They're estimating 10–30 concurrent users during trial, spikes to ~150 TPS on checkout flow. Sounds like burst capacity needed. Pricing note: sustained commit vs burst affects committed discount — sales will need numbers.
sam (DevEx): I'll draft minimal sample repos: node/ws stream example + python replay consumer. Also will add a structured-output schema example. Use this sample:
```json
{"order_id": "string", "items": [{"sku": "string", "qty": 1}], "fulfillment": {"method": "string", "eta_minutes": 30}}
```
jamie (SE): Perfect — add validation snippet and a fallback plan if model outputs don't match schema (we should show use of function-calling to enforce shape).
chris (Eng): For schema enforcement, show `function_call` with deterministic post-processing. Example: call name `emit_order_event` with args validated by server. Mention quantized model variant for cost savings on long histories.
security-bot: Cobalt shared their security questionnaire. Key items: data residency (EU), KMS integration, audit logs retention. They asked for SOC2 section & encryption-at-rest details.
legal: We need to review their DPA and run the SSO/KMS answers by security. Also confirm that POC doesn't require onboarding of production customer data. Add clause for trial data TTL.
maria (AE): Sales ask — can we provide an estimated per-checkout cost for the trial config (websockets, streaming, structured outputs, burst to 150 TPS for 2h/day)? They want an anchor number before the kickoff call.
chris (Eng): Quick napkin: streaming tokens per checkout ~350 tokens (prompt+responses+metadata), structured validation adds ~20 tokens. 150 TPS * 350 ~ 52.5k tokens/sec peak. If 2h/day for 5 days that's ~1.89e9 tokens; with hosted pricing that's expensive — recommend dedicated trial with burst credits. I'll sync numbers in a spreadsheet and post later today.
jamie (SE): I'll prep a runbook: handshake steps, ephemeral creds sample, & a small canary script to exercise function calls and validate JSON outputs.
sam (DevEx): Putting sample repos in the shared drive and will ping everyone when ready. Also adding a short troubleshooting checklist for common streaming issues (CORS, proxy timeouts, websocket pings).
maria (AE): Thanks. Can @legal and @security-bot confirm timeline to return signed POC DPA (they want to start Monday)?
legal: We can turn around a POC DPA template in 48 hours. Need to confirm EU data path and whether logs will include PII.
security-bot: Confirmed — we'll produce answers for KMS & retention in the next 24 hours. Also recommend offering EU-only region for this POC.
maria (AE): Great — jamie, chris, sam: please share the tech runbook + ballpark pricing by EOD. I'll update the customer and tentatively book kickoff Mon 10am CET. :thumbsup:
jamie (SE): On it.
chris (Eng): Will post numbers and config options.
sam (DevEx): Sample repos incoming.
